name: LongVid
description: A large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. The dataset contains 300,000 hours of videos and 2 billion words of textual annotations, supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios.

creator.name: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (Chinese Academy of Sciences), Shanghai Innovation Institute
creator.authors: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang

citeAs: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, et al. VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv:2501.00574v4, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets, including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-Vila, and MiraData, encompassing a wide range of video types: movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, and how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos of long duration. Dense event labels are generated for each long video by utilizing existing high-quality short video captions and filtering consecutive segments that can be regrouped into a long video sequence.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos are curated from 4 open-source video datasets: Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. For data curation, existing high-quality short video captions are utilized (Panda-70M for HD-VILA, CosMo for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D, and the original high-quality captions provided in MiraData).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Consecutive segments that can be regrouped into a long video sequence are filtered. A sequence of event labels with their corresponding timestamps is constructed for every long video based on their captions. For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), these are directly utilized as the event labels, while for others, the major event is extracted from the caption using an LLM.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duration-based sampling is performed on raw videos to obtain T frames as input. For short videos where D < Tmin, dense sampling is conducted to capture detailed motions. For long videos where D > Tmax, sparse sampling is performed to focus on event understanding. Videos are segmented into multiple clips, and each clip is encoded using a video encoder with spatio-temporal attention. Token merging is utilized to combine highly similar tokens, achieving compression to approximately 16 tokens per frame.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Several types of long video QA pairs are constructed based on the video captions, event labels, and the timestamps of short video segments. They are categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. For Ego4D, hierarchical captions from Ego4DHcap are used. For MiraData, an open-source LLM (Qwen-72b) is used to extract event and background labels. For HowTo100M, HTStep temporal annotations are used. For HD-VILA, captions from Panda-70M are utilized and event labels are extracted using an LLM.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple QA pairs per video across five task types
rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLM (Qwen-72b) for event extraction, existing caption models (Panda-70M, CosMo, Ego4D-HCap, MiraData captions)
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Fine Tuning. The dataset is used for multi-stage short-to-long learning to enable models to handle videos of different lengths and different types of tasks. Stage-3 of training involves joint short and long video instruction tuning using 0.7M long videos (60-3600 seconds) from the dataset.
